correctness.rationale: The GL finite-frame completeness premise is standard. Complementary modal selectors follow from finite transitivity/irreflexivity and existence of maximal successors. Non-selfdual f has a vector a with f(a)=f(not a), yielding a single-variable modal-depth-two uniform constant on every finite GL frame. Selfdual nondefinability is established by a structural induction constructing two finite transitive irreflexive models with opposite truth for every fragment formula, including modal nesting and all selfdual Boolean gates. Depth-one sharpness arguments use explicit 2-world frames and uniform valuations. The standalone checker runs exhaustive small-frame semantic tests, truth-table tests, and constructive witness tests; these are corroborative, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: A full-text comparison with the 2026 Modal Fragments paper found only a Type C Boolean-clone sandwich and the single OR-to-top example for GL, not an all-clones self-dual/no-constant iff criterion or the constructive contingency converse. The 2026 positive GL proof-system paper treats primitive constants, not absence of constants from bases. Direct statement/implication searches in research records and previously published mathematical results located no dominating theorem. The 2000 Rata–Rusu expressibility paper remains a specifically documented full-text access risk; no uniqueness claim follows from searches.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 survey isolates Type C modal Boolean-clone closure as incompletely characterized. This result gives an exact, basis-independent boundary across all positive-arity Boolean clones for the natural first obstruction—generation of Boolean constants in GL—with constructive depth-two witnesses and a uniform converse contingency theorem. It distinguishes selfdual bases such as majority/negation from nonselfdual bases such as conjunction/disjunction without proposing to settle full clone containment. The depth-two bound is independently sharp for fundamental Post bases.
